meta.label: Online courses
meta.attribution: Drawn from platform terms of use, refund policies, court and settlement records, the American Council on Education's National Guide to college credit recommendations, official accreditation and degree-awarding registers (the US Department of Education's College Navigator, CHEA's chart of recognised accreditors and the UK Office for Students Register), and app store price listings, not audited by us. Course platforms differ less on subject coverage than on what a certificate is worth once you leave the platform, what you get back if the course does not deliver, and whether the person teaching was paid or was giving the platform free labour. Where a platform's own pages could not be read directly, the score is left out rather than guessed. Suggest changes via Contribute.

criteria.label: Certificate or credit an outside body recognises
Refund or recourse if the course does not deliver
Whether the people teaching are paid or unpaid

products.name: Coursera
products.description: A large university and industry partner platform offering free audit access to many courses alongside paid Specializations, Professional Certificates and full online degrees.

economical.note: Coursera's own pricing page lists Coursera Plus at $59 a month, cancel anytime, or $399 a year with a 14-day money-back guarantee.

certification.note: Coursera's American Council on Education National Guide listing states Coursera has completed an ACE Learning Evaluations review to become an ACE Authorized Instructional Platform, with dozens of Professional Certificates from partners such as Google and IBM carrying ACE credit recommendations.

buyer_protection.note: Coursera's Terms of Use say you may receive a full refund if you cancel within 7 days of payment or before earning a certificate, whichever comes first; annual subscriptions must be cancelled within 14 days and renewal charges are not refunded; refunds are denied for Honor Code or Terms of Use violations or once a significant portion of the content has been accessed.

products.name: edX
products.description: A course platform founded by Harvard and MIT that keeps a free audit track on most courses alongside paid Verified Certificates; the edX business is now operated by 2U, a for-profit company that emerged from Chapter 11 bankruptcy in 2024.

economical.note: edX's own Terms of Service describe a free audit track alongside a paid Certificate Track, with refunds available for 14 days after payment for the certificate track and no refunds once a certificate is earned.

certification.note: The ACE National Guide lists edX with 9 active courses carrying ACE credit recommendations, from 3 to 18 credits, including Harvard's CS50x and an IBM full stack cloud development course, valid through 2026.

buyer_protection.note: edX's Terms of Service state Certificate Track refunds are available for 14 days after payment, Professional Education refunds for 2 days after the course starts, unused Program bundle entitlements for 6 months, no refunds on Subscription Offerings, and no obligation to refund once a Certificate is earned.

products.name: Udemy
products.description: A marketplace of individually priced courses from independent instructors, built around frequent discount pricing; instructor pay and pricing pages could not be read directly for this entry.

buyer_protection.note: A federal class action, Williams v. Udemy Inc. (N.D. Cal., case 3:21-cv-06489), alleged Udemy displayed fictitious original list prices with strikethrough formatting next to discounted sale prices for courses that were never sold at the full listed price; the case was later refiled in California Superior Court, San Diego County (case 37-2023-00003666-CU-BT-NC) and settled, with eligible buyers able to claim $4 for each course purchased during the class period, up to $40.

products.name: Udacity
products.description: A project-based tech skills platform built around paid Nanodegree programs, acquired by Accenture in 2024 and folded into its Accenture LearnVantage training business.

economical.note: Udacity's own announcement of its All Access subscription sets the price at $249 a month, or $846 for a four-month plan paid upfront, which it describes as a 15 percent saving, for access to its full Nanodegree and course catalog.

buyer_protection.note: Udacity's Terms of Use give students 7 days from initial purchase of a subscription or a single Nanodegree program to cancel and request a full refund, state fees are non-refundable outside that window, and limit refunds to one per student for the life of the account.

products.name: LinkedIn Learning
products.description: A subscription video course library bundled with LinkedIn Premium, whose main credential is a certificate of completion that can be shown on a LinkedIn profile rather than an accredited qualification.

certification.note: LinkedIn's own help page says that when you complete a course or learning path you can add the certificate and new skills to your LinkedIn profile and share the completion with your network, but that LinkedIn does not provide certificates for collections or individual videos.

buyer_protection.note: LinkedIn's refund policy states Premium subscriptions, including LinkedIn Learning, may be refundable within 7 days from the date the subscription is charged without Premium usage, and that EU citizens are entitled to a full refund during the 14 days after the subscription begins.

products.name: Skillshare
products.description: A subscription library of short creative and professional classes, with some classes free and a 30-day trial on paid membership; teacher payment pages could not be read directly for this entry.

economical.note: Skillshare's own app listing states a 30-day trial before payment is automatically charged, with membership pricing shown as $31.99 a month or $169.99 a year for one plan tier and $49.99 a month or $167.99 a year for another, alongside free classes available without a subscription.

products.name: MasterClass
products.description: A subscription of video lessons taught by well-known experts and public figures, sold as one flat annual membership rather than individual accredited courses.

economical.note: MasterClass's own app listing shows an Individual annual membership at $119.99, a Duo plan at $179.99 and a Family plan at $239.99, each an auto-renewing annual subscription; the listing makes no mention of a certificate for completing a class.

products.name: Khan Academy
products.description: A donor-funded nonprofit offering free K-12 and early college courses, with content built by a paid staff rather than sold per course.

economical.note: Khan Academy's own About page states its mission is to provide a free, world-class education to anyone, anywhere, describing itself as a free tool with over 840 free courses.

labor.note: Khan Academy describes itself as a 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization that relies on donor contributions to sustain its work, meaning content is produced by an employed, donor-funded staff rather than sold per learner to individual instructors.

products.name: MIT OpenCourseWare
products.description: A free, Creative Commons-licensed archive of course materials from thousands of MIT courses, with no enrollment and no credit or certificate attached.

economical.note: MIT OpenCourseWare's own About page describes it as a free and open collection of material from thousands of MIT courses, with no enrollment required and materials always available to browse at your own pace.

certification.note: MIT OpenCourseWare's About page states plainly that MIT does not offer credit or certification to users of OCW.

products.name: freeCodeCamp
products.description: A donor-supported nonprofit teaching programming through free, project-based curriculum and self-issued certifications, with the curriculum itself substantially built by unpaid volunteer contributors.

economical.note: freeCodeCamp's own About page states it is a tax-exempt 501(c)(3) donor-supported public charity and that every aspect of freeCodeCamp is 100 percent free, including the courses, projects and certifications.

certification.note: freeCodeCamp's own About page says learners earn free verified certifications through project-based learning, with each certification taking around 300 hours of self-paced work; these are freeCodeCamp's own certifications and are not listed as ACE-recommended college credit.

labor.note: freeCodeCamp's own contributor recognition page describes the curriculum, codebase and articles as built by thousands of volunteers, who are thanked with annual recognition such as invitations and merchandise rather than direct payment for their contributions.

products.name: StraighterLine
products.description: A low-cost online course provider built around transferring credit into a degree at a partner college, with courses individually reviewed by the American Council on Education and no refunds once purchased.

certification.note: StraighterLine's ACE National Guide organization listing states StraighterLine has conducted over 30 ACE Reviews of its courses and that students who complete approved courses receive credit when they enroll with a school in its network of regionally accredited partner colleges and through the ACE Credit transcription system, though each college still decides whether to accept the credit.

buyer_protection.note: StraighterLine's Terms of Use state that purchases of memberships and course enrollment fees are non-refundable and all sales are final, with a refund available only if a purchased product becomes unavailable.

products.name: Sophia Learning
products.description: A monthly-membership platform of self-paced courses designed for college credit transfer, with over 75 courses carrying an American Council on Education credit recommendation.

economical.note: Sophia Learning's own subscription plans page lists the monthly membership plan at $99, billed automatically each month.

certification.note: Sophia Learning's ACE National Guide organization listing states Sophia has developed and launched over 75 ACE-recommended courses since 2012 and has served more than 250,000 learners.

buyer_protection.note: Sophia's own Account and Billing tutorial states that if you are not satisfied within 30 days and have not completed any courses, you may request a refund.

products.name: OpenLearn
products.description: A free learning platform run by the UK's Open University, offering Statements of Participation and digital badges rather than formal qualifications.

economical.note: OpenLearn's own FAQ page states OpenLearn is a free learning platform, delivered by The Open University as part of its Royal Charter commitment to support the wellbeing of the community.

certification.note: OpenLearn's own FAQ page states OpenLearn does not award formal qualifications; learners who complete a course can earn a Statement of Participation, and some 24-hour courses also award a digital badge, but these do not carry any formal credit towards a qualification.

products.name: Alison
products.description: A free course platform funded by advertising, where the course itself costs nothing but a digital or printed certificate of completion is an optional paid extra.

economical.note: Alison's own help centre article states that as a social enterprise, Alison's goal is to make education as accessible as possible, which is why courses are free of charge, and that Alison earns revenue via advertising and optional paid certificates rather than charging for the courses.

buyer_protection.note: Alison's Terms and Conditions state that if the platform shows a digital certificate has been downloaded then no refund is possible, and that no refunds are available for unspent time on a monthly subscription.

products.name: Pluralsight
products.description: A subscription library of technology and IT skills courses with skill assessments and hands-on labs, aimed at working developers and IT staff rather than academic credit.

economical.note: Pluralsight's own individual pricing page lists plans running from $29 to $49 a month, or $299 to $449 billed yearly, and offers a 10-day free trial that includes the full course library, Skill IQ assessments, certification prep and guided learning paths.

products.name: Free through your public library
products.description: Many public libraries pay for patrons to use a professional course library such as LinkedIn Learning at no cost with just a library card, though the exact catalog and provider vary by library.

economical.note: LinkedIn's own page for the LinkedIn Learning for Libraries program describes offering libraries a catalog of over 16,000 professional courses for their patrons; the Los Angeles Public Library's own page for the program confirms LinkedIn Learning is free and easy to access with your library card and PIN, with more than 3,000 courses and 150,000 videos available.

products.name: DataCamp
products.description: A subscription platform of short interactive data science, AI and programming courses, with a free first chapter of every course and DataCamp's own certificates and certifications rather than college credit.

economical.note: DataCamp's App Store listing is free to download and lists in-app subscriptions including a Standard Yearly Subscription at $164.99 and a Standard Monthly Subscription at $43.00. DataCamp's own pricing page adds a free Basic tier covering the first chapter of every course, with Premium shown at a special price of $14 a month billed annually.

certification.note: DataCamp's own pricing page says Premium includes certificates and industry-leading certifications, which are DataCamp's own and partner credentials. DataCamp does not appear in the American Council on Education's National Guide list of organizations with college credit recommendations, so these credentials carry no college credit.

buyer_protection.note: DataCamp's Terms of Use say all fees are non-refundable unless the terms state otherwise. An individual plan can be cancelled at any time but stays active to the end of the paid term, with no refunds for partially used or unused periods. Top-up AI tutor credits are also non-refundable.

products.name: Codecademy
products.description: An interactive coding course platform owned by Skillsoft, with a free Basic plan and paid Plus and Pro subscriptions that add career paths, certification prep and Codecademy's own professional certifications.

economical.note: The App Store listing for Codecademy's free Codecademy Go app lists Plus at $29.99 a month or $178.99 a year and Pro at $39.99 a month or $239.00 a year. Codecademy's own pricing page adds an always-free Basic plan and quotes Plus at $14.99 a month and Pro at $19.99 a month when billed annually.

certification.note: Codecademy's pricing page says Pro members earn a professional certification by passing all exams in select career paths, and offers prep paths for outside exams from AWS, Microsoft, CompTIA and ISC2, which are taken and paid for separately. The professional certifications are Codecademy's own. Codecademy has no listing in the ACE National Guide.

buyer_protection.note: Codecademy's Terms of Service say you can cancel at any time but 'there are no partial or pro-rata refunds for cancellation'; you keep access until the end of the paid monthly or annual period. The terms say Codecademy may offer free trials to new and eligible returning subscribers, and its pricing page offers a free trial of Plus.

products.name: Brilliant
products.description: An interactive maths, science and coding practice app with a limited free tier and a Premium subscription. It deliberately issues no certificates or credit.

economical.note: Brilliant's App Store listing is free to download and lists in-app Brilliant Premium purchases priced from $19.99 to $149.99, plus a Premium with Tutor option at up to $191.99. Brilliant's own help centre says the free tier is limited to two concepts or practice sets a day, and Premium removes that limit.

certification.note: Brilliant's own help centre says it does not offer completion certificates, course credits, academic degrees or professional certifications. Its accreditation by the Accrediting Commission for Schools, Western Association of Schools and Colleges (ACS WASC) is accreditation from a body for schools and educational programmes, and Brilliant says it is not an accredited degree-granting institution.

buyer_protection.note: Brilliant's Terms of Use say 'All payments To Brilliant for the Services are nonrefundable', with no refunds for partially used subscription periods, and any refund is a voluntary courtesy. Its help centre adds that a self-serve refund option appears for some web subscriptions but not all.

products.name: Domestika
products.description: A marketplace of creative courses in illustration, design, crafts and photography. Courses are sold one at a time or through a Plus subscription that comes with course credits. Domestika pays for course production and pays its teachers, but it does not publish their revenue share.

economical.note: Domestika's App Store listing is free to download and lists in-app course purchases from $5.99 to $19.99, with Plus at $19.99 for one month. Domestika's own Plus page lists the yearly plan as a single payment of $164.50, and its Terms of Use say an annual plan grants 12 course credits.

certification.note: Domestika's own Plus page says Plus members who complete a course they have bought receive a personalised certificate signed by the teacher. This is a certificate of completion with no outside body behind it, and Domestika has no listing in the ACE National Guide.

buyer_protection.note: Domestika's Terms of Use (last updated July 2026) say that if you are not satisfied with a course within the first 14 days after buying it, Domestika will refund the full amount and remove your access. No refunds are processed after that, partial refunds are not offered, and purchases made through Apple or Google app stores follow the store's own refund policy.

labor.note: Domestika's own page for prospective teachers says teachers pay nothing, Domestika covers the course production costs, and teachers earn money from their course, paid through PayPal. The page does not publish the revenue share or rate, so the terms of pay cannot be checked.

products.name: Treehouse
products.description: A long-running coding and design video course subscription with a Techdegree bootcamp tier. A handful of its courses can earn transferable college credit through a partner, University Pathways International (UPI Study).

economical.note: Treehouse's own plans page lists Courses at $25 a month (or $20.83 a month billed annually), Courses Plus at $49 a month and the Techdegree at $199 a month. Every plan starts with a free 7-day trial, and there is no free tier.

certification.note: The ACE National Guide lists UPI Study, Treehouse's college credit partner, as an organization whose courses are recognised by ACE and NCCRS, including a Cybersecurity course. Treehouse's own college credit page lists four such courses: HTML and CSS, JavaScript, Cybersecurity and Python. Passing each course's final exam and project earns 3 credits, and the transcript costs $35 through Credly. Treehouse's own Techdegree certificate carries no credit.

buyer_protection.note: Treehouse's Terms of Service (last updated May 28, 2026) say a membership can be cancelled at any time but takes effect at the end of the current monthly or yearly commitment period, and 'You will not be entitled to a refund for any fees already paid.' The free 7-day trial is the only way to try it without paying.

products.name: Study.com
products.description: A large library of short video lessons and self-paced college-level courses with ACE and NCCRS credit recommendations, sold by subscription. Study.com's own pricing and refund pages block automated reading, so only its credit is scored here.

certification.note: Study.com's ACE National Guide organization listing describes its online, self-paced courses as earning widely transferable credit, and lists more than 50 Study.com courses with ACE credit recommendations, from accounting to SQL. Study.com's App Store listing for College Saver adds that its courses are also recommended for credit by NCCRS and are accepted at 2,000+ colleges, though each college still decides what it accepts.

products.name: Saylor University
products.description: A nonprofit, tuition-free online provider, formerly Saylor Academy, run through the Constitution Foundation, a 501(c)(3). It offers free self-paced courses, some with ACE credit recommendations, and tuition-free master's degrees accredited by a UK agency that US regulators do not recognise.

economical.note: Saylor University's own Tuition & Fees page says every course, all course materials and completion certificates are free and that its master's programmes charge $0 tuition. The only charge is a $5 proctoring fee per exam session or attempt when you want ACE-recommended credit or a degree.

certification.note: The ACE National Guide lists Saylor University with more than 40 courses carrying ACE credit recommendations, and Saylor's own credit page says partner colleges have agreed to accept them. Its master's degrees are accredited by ASIC, a UK agency, and its continuing education by IACET. Neither appears on CHEA's chart of CHEA- and US Department of Education-recognised accrediting organizations, so the degrees do not carry US-recognised accreditation.

products.name: The Odin Project
products.description: A free, open source full stack web development curriculum, maintained by volunteers and built around projects rather than certificates.

economical.note: The Odin Project's own About page describes a free, comprehensive curriculum that can be taken entirely online, with the website and curriculum completely open source.

certification.note: The Odin Project's FAQ answers whether you get a certificate on completion: 'We don't provide a certificate for course completion', and points learners to a portfolio of projects instead.

labor.note: The Odin Project's About page says the project is 'maintained and continually improved by a team of volunteers' and lists 5000+ contributors. Learners get help in a Discord community run by the maintainers with many other volunteers, so the teaching relies on unpaid labour, as at freeCodeCamp.

products.name: Maven
products.description: A marketplace for live, cohort-based courses and workshops taught by working practitioners. Courses are expensive, but Maven publishes both its refund guarantee and the share of each sale that instructors keep.

economical.note: A typical Maven course page, Forward Deployed Engineering Bootcamp, lists the course at $2,500 USD for a cohort with 10 live sessions. Other Maven cohort courses checked were priced at $2,499 and $3,000. Maven's free Lightning Lessons are short taster sessions, not full courses.

certification.note: Maven course pages such as this one offer a certificate of completion to share with your employer or on LinkedIn. No outside body recognises it, and Maven has no listing in the ACE National Guide.

buyer_protection.note: Maven's Satisfaction Guarantee help article says courses shorter than four weeks can be fully refunded up to the course midpoint, and 'Courses that run four weeks or longer: You are eligible for a full refund through the Week 2 end date'. One-day workshops can be refunded any time before they start, and self-paced courses within 14 days if less than 25% is completed. The guarantee covers only courses showing the Maven Guarantee badge.

labor.note: Maven's Getting paid help article tells instructors 'you'll keep 90% of your course earnings minus Stripe fees'. Maven takes a 10% fee on each paid enrolment, and nothing is charged until a student pays. Instructors set their own course prices.

products.name: Western Governors University
products.description: A private nonprofit, fully online university offering competency-based bachelor's and master's degrees at a flat price per term. It is institutionally accredited and employs its faculty, so it is a degree rather than a course subscription.

economical.note: The US Department of Education's College Navigator lists WGU as a 4-year private not-for-profit institution with undergraduate tuition and fees of $8,658 for 2024-2025, up from $8,300 the year before. WGU's own tuition page gives an average yearly bachelor's tuition of $8,300, about half the national average, but still far more per year than any course subscription.

certification.note: The US Department of Education's College Navigator lists WGU's institutional accreditation with the Northwest Commission on Colleges and Universities as current, accredited since 02/13/2003, with the next review due 10/01/2030. NWCCU appears on CHEA's chart as recognised by both CHEA and the US Department of Education. WGU awards full bachelor's and master's degrees.

buyer_protection.note: WGU's October 2026 Institutional Catalog gives a full refund, minus the application fee, to students who withdraw within three business days of their first term start, and a prorated tuition refund to withdrawals before 60% of a term is completed. 'Students with a withdrawal date occurring after 60% of the term is completed are not eligible for a refund.'

labor.note: WGU's October 2026 Institutional Catalog says 'WGU employs a disaggregated faculty model', splitting teaching into paid faculty roles such as curriculum, assessment, clinical and instructor faculty. The US Department of Education's College Navigator counts 3,576 full-time and 1,317 part-time instructional faculty for Fall 2024.

products.name: The Open University (degree modules)
products.description: The UK's distance-learning university, whose paid modules count toward full degrees and qualifications. It is separate from its free OpenLearn platform.

economical.note: The Open University's Fee Rules (Undergraduate) for England 2026/27 set the maximum it can charge England-fee undergraduates on a qualification at GBP 7,335 for a year of 120 credits or more, with a Fee Limit Discount applied if module fees exceed that. Part-time study costs proportionally less per module, but a degree still runs to thousands of pounds a year.

certification.note: The Office for Students Register lists The Open University (UKPRN 10007773) as registered in the Approved (fee cap) category. It holds research degree awarding powers and the right to use the university title, both dating from its 1969 Royal Charter, so its qualifications are UK degrees.

buyer_protection.note: The Open University's England 2026/27 Fee Rules give a right to cancel within 14 calendar days of registration being confirmed, and a full refund for cancelling any time before the module starts. Withdrawing before the 14th day of the module also carries no fee liability. After that, liability steps up to 25% and then 50%, reaching 100% only late in the module.
